review_notes: I read the whole file and checked the lemmas its simp calls use: convexHull_vadd and convexHull_smul in Convex/Hull.lean, AffineBasis.coe_vadd and coe_smul in LinearAlgebra/AffineSpace/Basis.lean, Set.range_smul in Algebra/Group/Pointwise/Set/Scalar.lean, and the interior_smul lemmas. The two distance lemmas near the top are only used by name, so I did not recommend simp attributes for them. The finding is about the ad hoc simp sets in the main lemma's proof. Without running Lean I cannot confirm that the proposed simp lemmas would be confluent with the existing ones or would shorten these calls, so I did not claim a loop or a simplifier failure.

findings.problem: There is no simp lemma saying that the range of a translated or scaled affine basis is the translated or scaled range. AffineBasis.coe_vadd and coe_smul are simp, so `range ⇑(x +ᵥ b)` becomes `range (x +ᵥ ⇑b)`. Each use then has to unfold `Pi.vadd_def` or `Pi.smul_def` by hand and re-fold with a pointwise-set lemma. The three simp calls (lines 54–57, 65–66, 85–86) each rebuild a different private mix of `convexHull_vadd`, `interior_vadd`, `Pi.vadd_def`, `mem_vadd_set_iff_neg_vadd_mem`, `range_add` and `range_smul`. The first call also has to switch `vadd_eq_add` off and then back on for one instance (`-vadd_eq_add, vadd_eq_add (a := -x)`), which is a symptom of competing rewrite rules. The same `interior_vadd` and `mem_vadd_set_iff_neg_vadd_mem` pair is also passed by hand in Mathlib/Analysis/Convex/GaugeRescale.lean, so this is not a one-off.
findings.proposed_change: Add simp lemmas next to `AffineBasis.coe_vadd` and `AffineBasis.coe_smul` for the ranges, for example `Set.range ⇑(v +ᵥ b) = v +ᵥ Set.range ⇑b` and the `smul` analogue. These can be proved by `Set.range_vadd` and `Set.range_smul`. Consider also marking `convexHull_vadd` and `convexHull_smul` as `@[simp]`, since each moves the pointwise action outward in a single direction. Then the three simpa calls reduce to the genuinely needed lemmas, such as `mem_vadd_set_iff_neg_vadd_mem` and `interior_vadd`. The `-vadd_eq_add` and `vadd_eq_add (a := -x)` workaround can be dropped.
findings.benefit: The translation and scaling steps would normalise to `x +ᵥ convexHull ℝ (range b)` by default, so the proofs no longer depend on hand-assembled simp sets that differ from call to call. Other users working with translated or scaled bases would get the same normal form.
